drhp.business: Khazanchi Jewellers is engaged in the wholesale and retail sale of gold jewellery, diamond jewellery and precious stone jewellery, built on an integrated model of sourcing, in-house design, manufacturing partnerships and retail operations. Wholesale (B2B) is the stable, cash-generating core serving more than 1,000 clients across India through an asset-light model using authorised partner manufacturers, while retail (B2C) is a smaller but faster-growing, higher-margin channel anchored by a new flagship showroom in Chennai.

drhp.expansion: Khazanchi's recent expansion has been retail-led rather than manufacturing-led, consistent with its asset-light model (manufacturing is outsourced to authorised partner manufacturers). risks.note: Gold and precious metals are the largest part of inventory and procurement cost; price volatility affects inventory values and margins. Mitigated by planning procurement against demand forecasts, keeping inventory tight, and opportunistic forward buying during price corrections.
The sector is subject to evolving rules on hallmarking, GST, import duty and KYC norms; changes in these rules can disrupt cost structures and operations.

The market is consolidating and national jewellery chains are expanding aggressively into South India, the Company's core market; it competes on design library depth, showroom experience and premium positioning (Vajraa, brand ambassador).
The business is working-capital intensive due to high gold inventory and seasonal demand; debt-to-equity rose from 0.28x to 0.35x during the year as current borrowings increased to fund inventory.
Tamil Nadu accounted for 75% of FY26 revenue and the retail footprint remains concentrated in South India, limiting brand visibility elsewhere even as other states' contribution has been rising.
risks.risk: Geographic concentration in Tamil Nadu / South India

risks.note: Retail is still a small part of total revenue (10% in FY26) compared with wholesale (90%), even though retail earns better margins, leaving profitability still heavily dependent on the lower-margin wholesale channel.
An economic slowdown or sustained inflation could reduce discretionary spending on jewellery, a category management explicitly flags as a threat.
